rails.name: USDC
rails.plain: A digital dollar issued by Circle. Businesses use it to send and settle payments on many blockchains, any time of day.

rails.name: USDT (Tether)
rails.plain: A digital dollar issued by Tether. Tether says each token is pegged 1-to-1 with a matching fiat currency and backed by its reserves. It runs on several blockchains.

rails.name: RLUSD (Ripple USD)
rails.plain: Ripple's dollar stablecoin. Ripple says it is approved by NYDFS and the DFSA, runs on the XRP Ledger, Ethereum and other networks, and is built into Ripple Payments in some regions.

rails.name: PYUSD (PayPal USD)
rails.plain: PayPal's dollar stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 for US dollars per PayPal. Inside PayPal it can be sent, converted, or spent where PayPal is accepted in the U.S.

rails.name: XRP / XRP Ledger
rails.plain: The XRP Ledger is an open-source public blockchain, and XRP is its native asset. Ripple Payments can use XRP as a bridge between two currencies in cross-border transfers.

rails.name: Stellar / XLM
rails.plain: A public network built for payments and issuing assets like stablecoins, live since 2014. XLM is its native asset. MoneyGram uses it to let people cash USDC in and out.

rails.name: XDC Network
rails.plain: An open-source, EVM-compatible blockchain aimed at trade finance and tokenized real-world assets. Its XDC Payments platform runs with Bridge for cross-border transfers.

rails.name: Hedera / HBAR
rails.plain: A public network for building fast, secure, compliant apps, per Hedera. HBAR is its native coin, and USDC also runs on Hedera as a native (HTS) token.

rails.name: XPR Network
rails.plain: A blockchain with @usernames, zero gas fees, and on-chain identity, per XPR Network. The Metal Pay app settles transfers on it.

rails.name: Zebec Network
rails.plain: A crypto payroll and payments network offering stablecoin payroll and Mastercard-powered crypto cards. Its payroll product runs on Stellar with MoneyGram cash-out.
